claims: The Masters uses a sudden-death playoff format if golfers are tied after 72 holes.
Players immediately play the 18th hole in the Masters sudden-death playoff.
If still tied in the Masters sudden-death playoff, players proceed to the 10th hole.
Players alternate between the 18th hole and the 10th hole in the Masters sudden-death playoff until a winner is decided.
The sudden-death playoff format at the Masters was adopted in 1976.
The sudden-death playoff format at the Masters has been used 12 times since 1979.
The hole rotation in the Masters sudden-death playoff starts with the 18th hole then the 10th hole then the 18th hole.
In the Masters sudden-death playoff, the first player to win a hole outright is declared the champion.
The last playoff at the Masters occurred in 2025.
Rory McIlroy defeated Justin Rose in the 2025 Masters playoff.
Previously, the Masters used an 18-hole playoff on Monday.
Before that, the Masters used a 36-hole playoff.
No sudden-death playoff in Masters history has gone beyond two holes.
